title: Stepped shaft in tension, D/d = 2, sharp shoulder (r = 0) (axisymmetric)
description:
Stepped round bar (shaft) with a shoulder, in axial tension. Axisymmetric problem.
Geometry file (STEP): the meridional half-section of the solid of revolution, drawn in the xy-plane: x is the radius (x >= 0, axis of revolution x = 0) and y is the axial coordinate z.
Purpose: a turned steel tension rod whose diameter steps from d = 20 mm to D = 40 mm. The step is SHARP as drawn (no fillet): the small cylinder meets the flat annular shoulder face in the plane z = 60 mm at a 90-degree inside corner. The small-diameter section runs from the end face at z = 0 to the shoulder; the large-diameter section runs from the shoulder plane to the end face at z = 120 mm.
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3.
Load: a total axial tensile force P = 31.416 kN, applied as a uniform axial traction (pulling outward) on the large end face z = 120 mm. The nominal stress on the small diameter, 4P/(pi d^2), is 100 MPa.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements. Model it as axisymmetric.
Supports: the small end face z = 0 is supported axially only: zero axial displacement, free to contract radially (a frictionless support).
Report (in an axisymmetric model, x = r and y = z):
  peak_stress_shoulder: the maximum value of the maximum principal stress s1 on the small-cylinder surface and the shoulder face, i.e. at the inside corner where they meet [Pa]; report it, and say whether you trust it;
  elongation: the average axial displacement of the large end face (z = 120 mm) [m].
